lookbackNote: Weekly Tier-2 cadence per routines.md targets roughly a 30-day window; extended lookback to 2026-05-09 (baseline/last-known scan date) used for candidate discovery since no prior Tier-2 scan-*.json exists in this repo to bound the window tighter. Only items with a fresh trigger event (publication, effective-date-window crossing, or binding guidance dated within the last ~30 days) were emitted as alerts.

sourcesAttempted.note: Tranche 2 of Privacy Act reform remains a Government commitment, no Bill introduced, no commencement date. Not a trigger event. Children's Online Privacy Code registration deadline (2026-12-10) noted but has not newly crossed a 90/60/30/7-day threshold this week; deferred to a future scan.

APPI amendment bill Cabinet-approved 2026-04-07, submitted to Diet — not yet enacted, does not meet trigger threshold (Trigger #1 requires enactment/signing/publication). Logged to digest-pending.md as a horizon/awareness item because it explicitly covers cookie IDs and device identifiers under a new consent-required category.

PIPA Amendment Act 21445 (promulgated 2026-03-10, effective 2026-09-11) — effective date now within the 31-90-day window from scan date, triggering Trigger #7. Written up as RW-2026-07-31-02 (HIGH). WebFetch on pipc.go.kr not attempted (standing .gov-domain 403 caveat); corroborated via 4 independent secondary sources including a Korea-market law firm.
no new binding guidance in window; Advisory Guidelines for Selected Topics last revised 2024-05-23, outside window

PDPC public consultation on cookie/consent guidelines closed 2026-03-23; draft guidelines expected ~8 months later (outside window, not yet published). Not a trigger event; watch item for a future scan.

GB/T 46903-2025 Personal Information Protection Compliance Audit Requirements, effective 2026-07-01, operationalizing the binding 2025-05-01 CAC Audit Measures with explicit consent-mechanism-adequacy audit scope. Written up as RW-2026-07-31-01 (MEDIUM). WebFetch on cac.gov.cn returned HTTP 403; corroborated via secrss.com plus 3 English-language law-firm trackers (KWM, Bird & Bird, Law.asia). Also surfaced: sector-specific 'Automotive Data Cross-Border Transfer Guidelines (2026 edition)' effective 2026-07-01 — narrow applicability, logged to digest-pending.md as LOW.
no in-window executive regulation or binding cookie guidance surfaced; PDPL Executive Regulations (Cabinet Decision 111/2023) remain the operative framework
Proposed PDPL Implementing Regulation amendments remain in public-consultation/proposed status (consultation closed 2025-05-27); no final adoption confirmed in window. Not a trigger event.
no new binding cookie guidance in window; POPIA cookie-consent practice (12-month consent validity, accept-all/reject-all parity) unchanged from prior baseline understanding

GAID 2025 (operational since 2025-09-19) remains the operative cookie-banner framework; only in-window item is a compliance-audit-return filing deadline extension (2026-03-31 to 2026-05-30), which is a procedural filing-date change, not a consent-mechanic change, and is now past. Not written up.
no in-window enforcement or guidance on cookies/consent surfaced; EU adequacy dialogue ongoing but non-binding
no in-window enforcement or guidance surfaced in either jurisdiction

sourcesAttempted.source: EU-US Data Privacy Framework / CJEU appeal (Case C-703/25 P)
sourcesAttempted.note: EDPB first-review report (2026-03-12) is outside the lookback window. A secondary blog claimed a 'US Supreme Court ruling on 2026-07-02' affecting DPF underlying safeguards (FISA Section 702 / PCLOB) — investigated directly and could NOT corroborate any such SCOTUS ruling via independent search (FISA 702 developments found were a failed House reauthorization vote and a FISC one-year certification, not a Supreme Court ruling). REJECTED as an unverifiable/likely-inaccurate single-source claim; not written up. Recommend flagging for a 72-hour recheck only if a second independent source surfaces.

Logged to digest-pending.md, not written up as a standalone MEDIUM+ alert.

alertsWritten.instrument: PIPA Amendment Act No. 21445 (10% revenue fine tier, CEO accountability, ISMS-P mandate)

operationalCaveats: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on cac.gov.cn and secrss.com in this run, consistent with the standing operational caveat for official/government-adjacent domains; China items in this scan are link-verified-by-reference and corroborated via multiple independent secondary sources but not directly retrieved from a primary document.
WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on ico.org.uk in this run; the UK item is corroborated via search-indexed summaries and a law-firm tracker (Kennedys Law) rather than the ICO page itself.

No PIPC (Korea), MeitY-equivalent, or other primary government source was directly fetched this run; all Tier-2 findings rely on WebSearch plus secondary-source corroboration per the documented 403 caveat. Recommend prioritizing an allow-list review for cac.gov.cn, pipc.go.kr, and ico.org.uk given repeated relevance to Tier-1/Tier-2 alerts.

This is the first Tier-2 scan run in this repository (no prior scan-*.json covering Tier 2 exists to bound the lookback window); lookback was extended back to the 2026-05-09 baseline/activation date for candidate discovery, but only items with a genuinely fresh trigger (recent publication or a freshly-crossed effective-date threshold) were emitted as alerts, to avoid re-alerting on items that would have been caught by an earlier (non-existent) prior run.
